PROBABILITY FUNCTIONS (p.937)
Special Values of L(h, k, \rho)
26.3.14  L(h, k, 0)=Q(h)Q(k)
26.3.15  L(h, k, -1)=0 \quad (h+k\geq0)
26.3.16  L(h, k, -1)=P(h)-Q(k) \quad (h+k\leq0)
26.3.17  L(h, k, 1)=Q(h) \quad (k\leq h)
26.3.18  L(h, k, 1)=Q(k) \quad (k\geq h)
26.3.19  L(0,0,\rho)=\frac14+\frac{\arcsin \rho}{2\pi}
L(h, k, \rho) as a Function of L(h, 0, \rho)
26.3.20  L(h, k, \rho)=L\left(h, 0, \frac{(\rho h-k)(\mathrm{sgn}\ h)}{\sqrt{h^2-2\rho hk+k^2}}\right)+L\left(k, 0, \frac{(\rho k-h)(\mathrm{sgn}\ k)}{\sqrt{h^2-2\rho hk+k^2}}\right)-\begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } hk>0 \text{ or } hk=0 \\ & \text{and } h+k\geq0 \\ \tfrac12 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
where sgn h=1 if h\geq0 and sgn h=-1 if h<0.
[FIGURE: nomograph -- a grid of \rho (y-axis, 0 to -1.0) against h (x-axis, 0 to 1.00), overlaid
with a family of diagonal curves labelled by values .01 through .07 on the right edge and
.08 through .24 along the top, each curve tracing a level set of L(h,0,\rho)]
FIGURE 26.2.  L(h, 0, \rho) for 0\leq h\leq1 and -1\leq\rho\leq0.
Values for h<0 can be obtained using L(h, 0, -\rho)=\tfrac12-L(-h, 0, \rho).
note: Mixed formula + figure page, 26.3.14-26.3.20 (bivariate normal L-function special values and reduction formula) followed by Figure 26.2, a large nomograph chart of diagonal curve families -- marked [FIGURE], axis labels/caption/the two formula lines under it kept since those are text, not curve data.
